items.title: Capture immutable starting roster and sign-up snapshots automatically
items.notes: Issue #133; #132/#134 deployed as eca481e on October 20 Eastern, included in this cumulative record. Required indexes verified READY before Functions, rules, Storage and Hosting deployment; all 16 Functions active. Build/lint, 674 unit and 2336 isolated rules/backend tests passed; receipts on #132/#134. Scheduler enabled daily at 21:00 America/New_York. Read-only logs verified October 24 delivery at 21:00:39 EDT, sweep completion at 21:00:43, HTTP 200, zero candidates/captured/failed/retry and checkpointAdvanced true. Successful empty-night delivery is not evidence of populated production capture; that remains a first-raid operational check. Immutable publication, durable retries and audit reconstruction tested locally; invalid history fails explicitly, with no standing-team fallback or mock-history migration. items.title: Display historical raid rosters separately from live team assignments
items.notes: PR #132 deployed with #134 as eca481e; both production domains matched built HTML/JS/CSS, with deployment receipts on #132/#134. Active members browse immutable published starting snapshots by team/size with roster, bench and on-demand invitations/signups. No attendance or in-raid editing. Local invented-data UI and rules/backend coverage verified access and publication behavior; authenticated production history behavior and populated production capture were not retested. Required indexes and daily Scheduler delivery verified; October 24 was a successful empty sweep. Included in this cumulative release record.

items.title: Support audited in-raid roster changes
items.notes: Leader adjustments must not overwrite the starting snapshot.

items.title: Add leader benching, capacity and raid-spot priority workflows
items.notes: Basic pre-start leader active/bench placement is now explicitly tracked in RAID-011; do not delay it behind in-raid changes. This item retains advanced bench/capacity/raid-spot priority workflows. Distinguish voluntary Bench responses from leader-assigned positions. Agree advanced capacity and Casual/Hardcore allocation policy before implementation; no automatic allocation in the initial planning slice.

items.title: Record attendance and show rolling three-month reporting
items.notes: GitHub issue #22 (B7) is assigned to stewartalex4-art; preserve that claim and coordinate before starting. Assignment alone is not evidence of implementation. Record actual attendance, roll alts up to mains and preserve the December 9 baseline. October 19 agreement: assigned bench raiders receive credit only after confirming readiness when prompted 30 minutes before start; implement evidence capture before calculating that credit, coordinating the request with RAID-006. Confirmation window, later promotion and voluntary-bench policy remain open. Members see their own percentage; leaders see everyone. Audited corrections and distinct voluntary responses/leader bench positions remain required; sign-ups and snapshots alone do not prove participation.

items.title: Send raid notifications and request bench readiness before start
items.notes: Planned Discord creation announcement invites members whose main is ready regardless of standing assignment; ready alts alone do not qualify invitations. Remind unconfirmed invitees 24 hours and 1 hour before start. Request readiness from that scheduled raid's assigned bench 30 minutes before start; confirmation is required for bench attendance credit (RAID-005), not inferred from sign-up. Settle confirmation-state targeting, late scheduling/rescheduling, response windows and reliable server delivery/retries. Not required for the initial in-app scheduled-raid planning slice.

items.title: Build raid buff and debuff coverage checklist
items.notes: GitHub #16 covers the first checklist; #27 tracks recurring verification despite its earlier closure. Initial checklist deployed in ec45641. User-authorized October 25 scope on feature/raid-armor-debuff-coverage: separate Faerie Fire and Curse of Recklessness from Sunder/Expose alternatives (25 standard requirements). Revised product decision accepts the catalog for planning: normal statuses and solid borders, no research-confidence warnings. Planning accepts displayed catalog effects while preserving specialization, talent uncertainty/assumptions, party limits, distinct-player demand and modeled conflicts. Available means eligible provider availability, not active spells. Research passes, sources/confidence and notes remain internal. Build/lint, coverage type-check, 781 unit and 301 coverage tests passed. Demo-emulator browser checks covered standing/scheduled 10/20/40, Leadership, actual Guild Leader/Raid Leader/Member accounts, light/dark desktop/narrow layouts and keyboard/touch/popover behavior. No backend/rules/dependency changes. Claim: stewartalex4-art in #27 comment 6405571755; current main/open PRs show no overlap. Shared changes isolated in their own commit. PR #161 ready for review; not merged or deployed. Remaining: recurring data, scope/exclusivity and description review at beta end, launch week and December 9; armor stacking/replacement and curse simultaneity research remains unresolved. Planning acceptance does not verify game facts.

items.title: Fix ten-zone audited raid edit expression-budget failure
items.notes: Deployed and verified before this cumulative release summary. Reduced validator cost without changing the ten-zone limit, authorization or audit checks. Regression coverage includes ten-zone creation, complete edits, cancellation/restore, malformed snapshots and forged audits.

items.title: Add All characters / Hide alts filter to the Raid Teams available roster
items.notes: Integrated through PR #65 and first deployed in 79736d9; included in the f42a14d release summary. Filters only the available roster and Add from guild roster lists using existing main/alt links. Assigned alts remain visible. Saved assignments, assigned team counts and buff/debuff coverage calculations remain unchanged.

items.title: Prevent same-player characters sharing a 10-player raid team
items.notes: Added to the canonical backlog during release reconciliation; source GitHub issue #95 (B10), implemented by stewartalex4-art in #110 and deployed in d0ef75d with live assets verified. Member picker, dropdown and drag-and-drop refuse main/alt and sibling-alt conflicts with an explanatory dialog and no write. Existing assignments remain unchanged, with conflicts highlighted. Different players' alts can share a team. Checks use stable roster IDs and main/alt links. Client-side validation only: optional Firestore enforcement was not implemented; stale concurrent clients or direct writes can bypass the check. No sign-up restriction or automatic cleanup.

items.notes: Issue #124; implementation PR #125 merged and deployed in 8665779. Independent standing teams and raid-specific teams/bench, persistent main-ready invitations, leader placement controls and member-readable rosters delivered. Absent/new unavailable events clear positions; later leader placement requires acknowledgment without changing responses. Build/lint, 658 unit and 2303 isolated rules/server tests passed. All 15 production Functions active; live HTML/JS/CSS verified on both domains; authenticated production placement writes were not exercised. Full contract and local browser evidence remain in ARCHITECTURE.md and #125. RAID-001 snapshot handoff to Alex remains to be coordinated; December 9 unchanged. Start snapshots, audited in-raid changes, Discord automation, attendance and advanced allocation remain separate work.

items.title: Show started and failed raid snapshots in Raid History
items.notes: GitHub issue #150; approved by the maintainer on the issue. Requested by the guild's loot owner. A raid's snapshot appears in Raid History as soon as it is started, with what has been written so far and a banner saying the list may be incomplete, and a failed capture shows plainly with its reason, instead of staying invisible until complete. Needs the snapshot read rule to accept a started or failed record (a rules change; the maintainer deploys) and a small visible failure record.

items.title: List every raid with its category in Raid History and let leaders mark a raid complete
items.notes: GitHub issue #168; approved by the maintainer on the issue ("Approved as proposed"). Requested by the loot owner. Every raid has one category: Scheduled, In Progress, Complete (a Guild or Raid Leader pressed Mark complete, or 5 hours have passed since its start, whichever comes first) or Cancelled (at any time). Built on feat/raid-categories, PR #177. A pure shared raidCategory (src/shared/raids/raidCategory.ts) is used by Scheduled Raids and Raid History. firestore.rules accept raid status 'complete' only from Guild and Raid Leaders, after the saved start, never straight from cancelled, with an audit entry whose action is 'complete'; undo is an audited edit back to scheduled. Scheduled Raids chips say In Progress, Complete or Cancelled, and an opened row of a raid in progress has Mark complete (Undo complete once marked) for leaders. Raid History opens on All raids: every raid newest first from data already loaded (no new Firestore read), with category, month and phase filters and Show more; Audit Info is unchanged. The daily snapshot sweep still captures a raid marked complete. Phase filter (loot owner, 2026-10-29: give each loot phase a start date): settings keep phaseStarts, one Eastern date per finished and current phase; starting a phase records today, reopening removes it, and a Guild Leader sets or corrects dates in Settings > Loot phases, each an audited phase entry ('edit'); the rules refuse dates that go backwards. A raid is in the latest phase that started on or before its date. Remaining: the failed-capture warning (needs RAID-015's readable failure record) and a count of reads on opening Raid History. Coordinate with RAID-015 (#150), RAID-014 (#149) and proposed RAID-020, which also changes raid status values.

items.title: Show scheduled raids as collapsible banners with zone artwork
items.notes: GitHub issue #146; approved by the maintainer on the issue. Requested by the guild's loot owner. Scheduled Raids becomes a list of collapsed rows with no dropdown: each has a banner of its raid's zone pictures (every zone, side by side, each fading into the next; a color tint for a zone without a picture) and the raid's name, date, time and status. Opening a row shows today's roster, sign-ups and buff coverage and starts that raid's listeners only. Add Raid and Edit Raid show the zone pictures. A new shared banner in src/shared/raids/. On the first-raid path (Dec 9): land after RAID-013 and leave the roster workbench untouched. No rules or data change. Built on feat/scheduled-raid-banners: a shared RaidBanner and raidZoneArt (a raid zone's picture is found from its stored id; the small copy is used and loaded lazily), rows in features/scheduled-raids/ (RaidRow, groupRaids), and Add Raid and Edit Raid show each zone's picture and a banner preview. A row mounts its panel only while open, so closed rows start no listener. A raid is listed from the moment it is scheduled until 5 hours after its start, then leaves the list (Raid History keeps it); this replaces the issue's collapsed group of past raids, per the loot owner on 2026-10-27.

items.title: Show zone pictures on the upcoming raids of My dashboard
items.notes: GitHub issue #154; approved by the maintainer on the issue. Requested by the guild's loot owner. Each upcoming raid on My dashboard shows its zones' pictures, using the shared banner of RAID-016 (no new reads). Follows RAID-016 and MEMBER-006. Built on feat/dashboard-raid-art: each upcoming raid row gets a 40px strip of its zones' pictures (the shared RaidBanner; a zone with no picture shows its color tint), placed first by CSS with the strip as the row's last child so no existing child moves; the text and the sign-up button stay on the plain surface. Feature-local (src/features/dashboard): no data, rules or read change. Checked in the local emulators as a Member: rows with no zones and with 1, 2, 3 and 10 zones, the unavailable state, the sign-up dialog, View on calendar, light and dark, 375px and 320px. Not checked: a screen reader, Firefox, Safari.

Agree formats, duplicate detection and recipient matching. Preserve original award dates separately from later entry/audit timestamps. Support recovery of December 9 spreadsheet receipts. items.title: Complete main/alt priority policy and alt-only-run controls
items.notes: Not being built for now (2026-10-27): the loot owner decided the mains-over-alts rule is guild policy, not something the site needs to enforce. PR #163 and issue #162 are closed; the branch feat/mains-first-warning stays on the fork. Reopen if the guild wants the warning. Earlier notes, for reference: Priority adoption is expected around December 15. Confirm wording and per-raid exception; priorities are not required for initial loot recording. Decided by the loot owner (2026-10-24): mains get loot priority over alts, shown as a warning only (a leader sees, for example, that two mains still need the item and decides), not enforced; the alt-only exception is a tick in the Award loot and Record loot dialogs that silences the warning for that award (client only; the reason goes in the award note), for runs of any size; wording "Mains get loot prio over alts".

Remaining loot-data/filter research stays open in LOOT-007 and is not implied complete by this workflow release.

items.title: Let leaders upload zone artwork and choose a picture for each zone
items.notes: GitHub issue #115; PRs #116 and #117 merged. Client, Firestore and Storage rules deployed through 8665779; live HTML/JS/CSS verified on both domains. Guild Leaders manage a zone-image library and choose title banners for Loot priorities, Browse drops and the editor. Storage setup and cross-service access were confirmed in the #116 maintainer handoff; authenticated production upload remains untested. No artwork added to the repository. Per-boss pictures remain out of scope.

items.title: Filter the Carry over and Loot Drops dialogs by dungeon, boss and item slot
items.notes: GitHub issue #118; PRs #120 and #121 merged and deployed through 8665779, with live HTML/JS/CSS verified. Carry over filters by dungeon/boss and item slot without losing hidden selections; Browse drops filters by creature and item slot. Clear filters and shown counts delivered. Add all/Remove all still act on the whole zone. Player filters, persistent filters and an All zones view remain out of scope.

items.title: Add a candidate by ticking its box in Edit loot priority
items.notes: GitHub issue #119; PR #122 merged and deployed through 8665779, with live HTML/JS/CSS verified. Ticking adds candidates immediately; unticking removes the last listing and ticking straight back restores its place. Plus adds a repeat listing. Saved data, audit log and rules unchanged. Drag-and-drop ordering remains out of scope.

items.title: Show the loot phase on every Log entry and filter the Log by phase and by raid night
items.notes: Existing mapping from issue #141 retained without changing priority/target. PR #143 deployed via Hosting in fa95142 on October 24; receipt on #143. Phase column, phase search/filter and raid-date filter delivered. Awards use awardedAt; other entries use their entry day. Unknown phase shows a dash. Build/lint and 769 unit tests passed for the combined release; production assets matched on both domains. Filters apply to loaded entries (newest 100 first; Load older entries goes further back). An award stores no raid link: Date plus dungeon/boss distinguishes different dungeons, not two runs of the same dungeon or missing dungeon data. A stored raid link remains deferred until needed; if built, 20- and 10-player raids are separate pre-scheduled events, larger first, with audited leader reassignment. Client only; included in this cumulative release record. Mapping confirmed by the maintainer in the linked issue, as recorded in #158.

items.title: Add Removed member status and no-access screen
items.notes: GitHub issue #14 (A5), resolved by #75. Deployed in a36ba48 and verified; included in this cumulative release summary. Guild Leader-only removal/restoration with confirmation, no self-removal, atomic unlinking, backend access denial and live no-access screen. Characters, assignments, history and Auth account remain. Restoration grants unlinked Member access, requiring explicit relinking/promotion.

items.title: Add character-change requests and leader approvals
items.notes: Deployed in 0c8c9c9 and production-confirmed by maintainer; included in the 92dbc71 summary. Members submit/withdraw private alt-link, rename, class/spec and main-promotion requests. Guild Leader review moved from Member access to Leadership Overview in the 2026-10-18 release (MEMBER-003); members retain personal requests on My dashboard. Atomic approvals recheck ownership/snapshots and preserve IDs, teams and history. Decisions are in resolved history, without automatic notification. Stable-ID loot now follows renames (LOOT-003); legacy name-only records are not retroactively migrated.

items.title: Build leadership dashboard with per-character raid readiness
items.notes: Scope approved in #106; #108 deployed with rules before Hosting in b31493a; #111 confirmation deployed in d0ef75d, with live assets verified. Guild Leader-only Leadership Overview between Loot priorities and Member access: summary counts, missing responses, private character-request review and selected-raid current-assignment coverage with 10/20/40 selector. Per-character readiness defaults false; members manage main/direct alts on My dashboard, Guild Leaders manage flags in roster. Confirm saves; Cancel leaves the flag unchanged. Exact-field writes and reciprocal ownership are enforced by Firestore rules. Count each active linked account once when any owned character is ready; any response counts, with separate unready-attending warnings. Excluded/setup counts and coverage uncertainty remain visible. No sign-up restrictions, reminders, attendance, automatic benching or starting snapshots. Roster comments remain MEMBER-004.

items.title: Review dashboard comments from the roster
items.notes: Deployed first in 537f5d8 and confirmed by the maintainer; included in the ec45641 release summary. Scroll dismissal follow-up is UX-003.

items.title: See earlier phases' loot on My dashboard
items.notes: GitHub issue #157; approved by the maintainer on the issue ("As proposed is good", 2026-10-27). Requested by the maintainer's comment on #152 and agreed with the guild's loot owner. Checked in the local emulators as a Member and a reserve account with three phases: the picker, each phase, the reset on reload and on a new phase, the empty messages, no Firestore request or browser storage write, light and dark, 375px and 320px. items.title: Loot priorities: feature the item first on desktop
items.notes: GitHub issue #147; approved by the maintainer on the issue. Requested by the guild's loot owner. At 1101px and wider the item is twice its size (name 22px, icon 40px), the boss heading goes from 11px to 13px, and each card is three columns: the item alone, where it drops over the council note, then the council order with the leader buttons under it. items.title: Erase the pre-launch test data once, at launch, with a maintainer-run script
items.notes: GitHub issue #142, PR #159: the maintainer agreed to a one-time maintainer-run script, its scope (that phase's awards, loot priorities and the Log entries about them) and the AGENTS.md exception; the maintainer confirms the ID, priority and target. The maintainer runs it when the first real phase starts (launch), with the loot owner on a call reading the dry run's numbers; a full Firestore export comes first. Requested by the guild's loot owner: everything recorded in Launch prep was beta and testing and should not count, appear on dashboards or sit in the permanent record once the first real phase starts; the Log is immutable from then on. The rules (and AGENTS.md) never allow an award or Log entry to be deleted, so this is a script the maintainer runs once with the Admin SDK, not an app feature: dry run by default, confirmed counts and project, a typed phrase, a backup file read back before any delete, a guard that only the finished phase is erased, a check that nothing is left, then a seal and a visible Log record, and a refusal to run twice. Erases that phase's awards, loot priorities and the Log entries about them; keeps everything else. Built and tested on the local emulator with invented data; never run on a real project. See docs/design/launch-reset.md. Merged in #159; Log display support awaits Hosting deployment. Maintainer rehearsal/adoption and the one-time production reset have not been performed; do not mark the reset released from a merge or Hosting deploy.
